### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4e735824a580877f540c0c3a72ae6b2272e20a9b` — the merge of head `58a8f45bd2a8e861677ccf95272d028eb36810fa` into base `f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4e735824a580877f540c0c3a72ae6b2272e20a9b && git checkout 4e735824a580877f540c0c3a72ae6b2272e20a9b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c 58a8f45bd2a8e861677ccf95272d028eb36810fa && git checkout -B drift-repro f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c && git merge --no-ff 58a8f45bd2a8e861677ccf95272d028eb36810fa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `58a8f45bd2a8e861677ccf95272d028eb36810fa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook.metadata-form.ts + packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-declared-rows.pin.test.ts

Inputs read: card #36799 (body and all five comments), PR #38078 (body, four-file list, net diff from merge base `815e882b`), and the 69 check-runs on this head: 58 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed. The remainder of the diff (`packages/lint/src/validate-predicate-path-refs.test.ts`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`HookSchema` accept set: unchanged — right.** `hook.zod.ts` is not in the diff. What a hook may declare is exactly what it was.
- **Served `hookForm` (public surface of `@objectstack/spec`, via `METADATA_FORM_REGISTRY`): the `refusals` and `texts` rows each gain `visibleWhen: { dialect: 'cel', source: "data.body.language == 'js' || data.body == null && data.handler != null && data.handler != ''" }` — right.** No row is added, removed, renamed or retyped; labels and help text are untouched, so no locale pack moves.
- **What the Studio offers narrows to what the schema accepts — right.** Read against both refinements at this head (`refuseUndeclaredLiteralRefusalCode` and `refuseUndeclaredLiteralTextKey`: `answered = body === undefined ? hasHandler : body.language === 'js'`, with `hasHandler` a non-empty string): the predicate and the schema agree on a `js` body (shown), an `expression` body (hidden), a handler with no body (shown), neither (hidden), an empty handler (hidden), and also on the shapes the pin does not list: a handler beside an `expression` body (hidden, refused), a handler beside a `js` body (shown, accepted), and a present body with no `language` (hidden, refused). The schema's `typeof handler === 'function'` half has no counterpart, correctly: a form draft is JSON and cannot hold one.
- **Lint corpus census 96 → 98 predicates and 67 → 71 single-quoted comparisons — right.** Two new predicates, each with `== 'js'` and `!= ''`; the two `null` comparisons are not quoted literals. `Test Core (6/10)` is green on this head.
- **Generated output: none owed.** No generated file is in the diff and the lint and liveness gates are green.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: patch` matches what the diff publishes: a fix to a served form in a released package, no change to what a metadata author can write. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no key, value or requirement moves), and `none` takes `patch`. `Check Changeset` is green.

Clause-②: no — stated identically on the PR body and the changeset body, with no arm. Agreed: the accept set neither widens nor narrows; the diff changes only when two form rows are drawn.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev flag A — the Studio evaluator fails open on a parenthesised group.** Answered: filed as #38070 (open, p2, `domain:ui`). Confirmed in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/predicate.ts` at this head: a group's left side is read as the path `(data`, whose root is not in scope, which throws and is answered `true`. The hook predicate is written without parentheses and does not depend on #38070 either way: it reads the same if that card adds grouping or makes unreadable predicates fail closed.
- **Dev flag B — a hidden row keeps its value** (fill `refusals` on a `js` body, switch the body to `expression`: the row disappears and the save is refused at a key the form no longer draws). Answered: accepted for this PR. It is the form engine's behaviour for every `visibleWhen` row (the action form's `refusals` and `texts` rows gated on `data.type == 'script'` behave the same), and its fix lies in the Studio, outside this diff. Escalated to the seat: it is recorded only in the PR's acceptance notes and has no card; one should be filed so the behaviour is decided rather than inherited.
- **Seat flag — `dispatch-gates` did not derive `@objectstack/lint`'s tests from a `packages/spec` `*.metadata-form.ts` edit**, which is why the corpus census went red in CI rather than locally. Answered: not this PR's to fix. Escalated to the seat: the claim amendment says "reported, not fixed here" and names no card; it needs one.
- **SQL push-down:** not applicable. The diff reads no data, materialises no ids and joins nothing.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/hook.metadata-form.ts`** — holds against the card's ask, the schema it mirrors and its first consumer.

- Against the card: the ask is a `visibleWhen` on both rows "matching the schema's own test", in the dialect the other metadata forms use. Both rows carry one shared constant, so they cannot drift from each other. The spelling follows shipped precedent (`view.metadata-form.ts` already compares `data.type == null`).
- Against the first consumer, read in `predicate.ts` at this head: `||` is split before `&&`, so the sentence parses as `A || (B && C && D)` with no grouping needed; `data.body.language` on an absent body resolves to `undefined` and compares false, not a fault, because the root `data` is always bound; `== null` is loose over `null` and `undefined`; `!= ''` parses the empty quoted literal. `data.handler != null` is not redundant: without it an absent handler would satisfy `!= ''`.
- Attempts to break it: (1) a draft the form writes as an empty body — `compositeWith` in `SchemaForm.tsx` removes a composite left empty when its schema requires a key with no default, so clearing the body returns the draft to "no body", and if a `{}` body did reach the draft, the predicate and the schema still agree (hidden, refused). (2) A handler beside an `expression` body — hidden, and the schema refuses it there. (3) Precedence under a real CEL reader — `&&` binds tighter than `||` there too, so the grouping is the same. A strict CEL runtime would treat a missing `data.body` as a fault where the interim evaluator reads `undefined`, but that is true of every shipped `data.x == ...` row on an unfilled draft and belongs to the evaluator swap, not to this row.
- The docblock, sentence by sentence: "a `js` body, or no body and a handler" — agrees with both refinements; "the handler half reads non-empty, as the schema's does" — agrees (the schema requires a string of non-zero length); "splits `||` before `&&` but has no grouping, and a parenthesised group fails open" — agrees with `evalExpr`, `splitTopLevel` and `resolveValue`. The form's own docblock now says the rows are shown only where `HookSchema` accepts them, which is what the tree does.

**`packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-declared-rows.pin.test.ts`** (the enforcing pin) — agrees with the contract. Its local reader matches the Studio evaluator on the subset used (same split order, same loose null equality, left-side paths only) and throws on any other shape, with a control for a grouped and an `in` rewrite. The served predicate is pinned by exact equality per row, and `refusedAt` reads the schema's verdict from the issue path, with a control that the schema cut is real in both directions.

N1 (nit) — the pin's docblock says it holds the predicate equal to the schema "on each draft shape the form can produce", but the five drafts omit a handler beside an `expression` body, which the form can produce and which is the one shape that exercises the `data.body == null` atom on its own: deleting that atom leaves all ten draft cases green. No effect on correctness or the contract — the exact-source equality pin catches that rewrite, and the tree is right on that shape. Left as an accepted deviation; a sixth draft can ride any later touch of the file.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38078/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
